original_query: SELECT CAST(1 AS INTEGER) AS DEPTNO, ENAME FROM (SELECT ENAME FROM (SELECT ENAME, DEPTNO FROM EMPNULLABLES) AS t6 WHERE DEPTNO = 1 UNION ALL SELECT ENAME FROM (SELECT ENAME, DEPTNO FROM EMPNULLABLES) AS t9 WHERE DEPTNO = 1) AS t12
rewritten_query:
SELECT CAST(1 AS INTEGER) AS DEPTNO, e.ENAME
FROM EMPNULLABLES e
CROSS JOIN (VALUES (1), (1)) AS d(x)
WHERE e.DEPTNO = 1;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Flatten redundant derived tables t6, t9 and t12; the DEPTNO = 1 filter can be applied directly against EMPNULLABLES.

Replace the UNION ALL of two identical scans of EMPNULLABLES with a single scan duplicated via CROSS JOIN (VALUES (1), (1)), preserving the double-output semantics while avoiding a 45M-row table being scanned twice.

Since DEPTNO = 1 appears to be highly selective (estimate ~78 rows out of 45M), consider a covering index: CREATE INDEX ON EMPNULLABLES (DEPTNO) INCLUDE (ENAME) to replace full sequential scans with index scans.
